Based on my analysis of the agreement (Gray Television / Meredith, dated May 3, 2021):

The Fiduciary Termination Right is **Section 9.1(d)(ii)**, governed by **Section 7.3(e)**. The relevant text reads:

"...in the case of a Company Acquisition Proposal that was unsolicited after the date of this Agreement and **that did not result from a material breach of this Section 7.3**, terminate this Agreement pursuant to Section 9.1(d)(ii) ... in order to enter into a definitive agreement in connection with **a Superior Company Proposal**..."

So the FTR is limited by:
1. **Material** breach of the no-shop (Section 7.3) resulting in a Superior Offer (note Section 7.3(b) uses only "breach" for discussions/info, but the FTR provision specifies "material breach"), and
2. The need for a Superior Company Proposal.

There is no condition requiring the absence of breach of *other* provisions for the FTR. This matches choice **A**.
